hypotheses.reasoning: The 503s on POST /login come from account-svc's calls to auth-svc POST /tokens. Auth-svc was healthy (ok ~20-80ms) until about 11:09:30. Then it began returning 503s and load-shedding ('queue full'), and its inbound rate reached 3.2x-5x baseline with 700+ requests in flight. Account-svc's AuthClient retry policy has backoff and jitter disabled: it retries 503s immediately, up to 4 attempts (#3126, #3304, #3443, #3587). Each failed login therefore sends several more requests to auth-svc at once. That amplification keeps auth-svc saturated, so it never recovers, and edge-proxy surfaces the exhausted retries as 503s (#3208 onward). The trigger is a load spike on auth-svc whose exact source I could not pin down. The amplifier is the immediate-retry policy with no backoff. Report-cron (missing pandas module since image 2026.10.2, #1068) and status-poller (timeouts to deprecated legacy-inventory, #908) are real errors but unrelated: they do not touch the login path. Accounts-db and session-cache are healthy.

Alternative reading: auth-svc's own request queue or inflight limit is too small for this traffic, so it saturates and load-sheds ('queue full', 732 inflight). The GC and heap logs look normal, so this is less likely than the retry amplification, but a queue limit that is too small would explain the same lines.

verdict.recommendedAction: Re-enable exponential backoff with jitter and cap retries in account-svc's auth-svc RetryPolicy, rolling back whatever disabled it if that change was recent. Shed or rate-limit login traffic at edge-proxy so auth-svc can drain its queue. Scale auth-svc or raise its admission limits. Separately, find what drove the inbound spike to auth-svc around 11:09, fix the report-cron image (missing pandas), and point the status-poller healthcheck away from the deprecated legacy-inventory endpoint.

hypotheses.reasoning: The 503s on POST /login come from account-svc's calls to auth-svc POST /tokens. Auth-svc was healthy (ok ~20-80ms) until about 11:09:30. Then it began returning 503s and load-shedding ('queue full'), and its inbound rate reached 3.2x-5x baseline with 700+ requests in flight. Account-svc's AuthClient retry policy has backoff and jitter disabled: it retries 503s immediately, up to 4 attempts (#3126, #3304, #3443, #3587). Each failed login therefore sends several more requests to auth-svc at once. That amplification keeps auth-svc saturated, so it never recovers, and edge-proxy surfaces the exhausted retries as 503s (#3208 onward). The trigger is a load spike on auth-svc whose exact source I could not pin down. The amplifier is the immediate-retry policy with no backoff. Report-cron (missing pandas module since image 2026.10.2, #1068) and status-poller (timeouts to deprecated legacy-inventory, #908) are real errors but unrelated: they do not touch the login path. Accounts-db and session-cache are healthy.
hypotheses.recommendedAction: Immediately re-enable exponential backoff with jitter and cap retries in account-svc's auth-svc RetryPolicy (roll back the change that disabled backoff, if one was recent). Shed or rate-limit login traffic at edge-proxy to let auth-svc drain its queue. Scale auth-svc capacity or raise its admission limits. Separately trace what drove the inbound spike to auth-svc at about 11:09, and fix the report-cron image (missing pandas) and the status-poller healthcheck pointing at the deprecated legacy-inventory endpoint.

hypotheses.reasoning: Alternative reading: auth-svc's own request queue or inflight limit is too small for this traffic, so it saturates and load-sheds ('queue full', 732 inflight). The GC and heap logs look normal, so this is less likely than the retry amplification, but a queue limit that is too small would explain the same lines.

input.recommendedAction: Re-enable exponential backoff with jitter and cap retries in account-svc's auth-svc RetryPolicy, rolling back whatever disabled it if that change was recent. Shed or rate-limit login traffic at edge-proxy so auth-svc can drain its queue. Scale auth-svc or raise its admission limits. Separately, find what drove the inbound spike to auth-svc around 11:09, fix the report-cron image (missing pandas), and point the status-poller healthcheck away from the deprecated legacy-inventory endpoint.
